 JUDGMENT Smt. Sunitha claiming to be guardian of her husband Nagaraju filed petition under Sec.166 of I.M.V.
Act on behalf of Nagaraju claiming compensation worth of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents who are insurer and owner of a car No.KA-50-A-9858 asserting that 02.08.2021 at 10.30 AM when Nagaraju riding a motorcycle No.KA-54- L-5977 from Peenya towards Sahakarnagar by keeping Mr.
Ramachandra on pillion on Hebbal Ring Road, near Hebbal Lake
, driver of car No. KA-50-A-9858 negligently drove the same dashed the same to the motorcycle thereby caused accident caused injuries to the petitioner.
Nagaraju took treatment at NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru, Government Hospital, Hassan, Mangala Hospital, Hassan by spending Rs.5,00,000/-.
As on the date of the accident Nagaraju being aged 34 years use to earn Rs.25,000/- per month by working as Electrician.

Regarding the accident Hebbal Traffic Police registered Crime No.77/2021 against the driver of car for having committed the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 of IPC.
2.

In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by Nagaraju, age, occupation and income of Nagaraju.
3 Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.2 owner of the car remained absent.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 19.02.2022 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of Swift Dzire Car bearing registration No.KA-50-A-9858 by its driver dashed to the petitioner who was riding the motor cycle bearing No. KA-54-L-5977 and he sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 2.08.2021?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of petitioner himself?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
4.
What order?
5. On 16.01.2024, 19.01.2024 Sunitha W/o Nagaraju deposed as PW.2 and get produced 12 documents at Exs.P.5 to P.16.

On 04.03.2023, 03.06.2023 Sunitha produced evidence of Dr. Shailesh as PW.1 and get produced 4 documents at Exhibits P.1 to P.4.

REASONS 8. Issue No.1 & 2:- In the lengthy arguments learned advocate appearing for the petitioner by analyzing the evidence in the file requested to answer Issue No.1 in favour of the petitioner and award reasonable compensation.
9. In the lengthy arguments learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.1 by analyzing the evidence affidavit in the file respondent No.1 requested to answer Issue No.2 in favour of the insurance company and dismiss the petition by relying on the following judgments:-
a) MFA No.23491/2012 - The Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd., vs The North West Karnataka Road Transport DD 16th November 2021 - High Court of Karnataka Para 9 onwards b) 2005 ACJ 1332 - Harkhu Bai and ors. vs. Jiyaram and ors. DD 10th July 2003 - High Court of Karnataka Para 4.

sentences.text: In the light of the submission made on behalf of both contesting parties with reference to judgment cited above, I have appreciated the materials available in the file.

11. In the evidence affidavit, PW.2 Sunitha W/o Nagaraju stated that she came to know that on 02.08.2021 at 10.30 AM when Nagaraju riding the motorcycle No.KA- 54-L-5977 by keeping Ramachandra on the pillion from Peenya towards Sahakarnagar on the road near Hebbal Lake,
driver of car No.KA-50-A-9858 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the motorcycle No.
KA-54- L-5977 thereby caused accident and caused injuries to Nagaraju.
12.
In the written statements, respondent No.1 insurance company denied the allegation regarding the reason and mode of accident.

13. In the cross-examination, PW.2 stated that she never witnessed the accident and Ramachandra employer of her husband (pillion rider) has filed the complaint after two days of the accident.

Ex.P5 and P6 are the copy of FIR and complaint pertaining to Crime No.77/2021 registered by Hebbal Traffic Police on 04.08.2021 against the driver of the car No. KA-50-A-9858 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279 & 337 of IPC, regarding the accident taken place between motorcycle No. KA-54-L-5977 and car No.KA-50-A-9858 resulting in the injuries to the Nagaraju on the basis of the complaint presented by Ramachandra on 04.08.2021 at 17.20 hours.
15. Ex.P7 is the copy of the spot mahazar recorded on 05.08.2021.
Ex.P8 is the copy of sketch which shows that on West-East road, the collision taken place between motorcycle and the car which are running in the same direction.

Ex.P9 is the Motor Vehicle Accident Report dated 05.08.2021.
16.
Ex.P10 is the copy of the Wound Certificate in which reason for the injuries are noted as RTA two wheeler vs. four wheeler on 02.08.2021 at 10.30 in Hebbal.

sentences.text: Ex.P11 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Hebbal Traffic Police in crime No.77/2021 against Vinod Kumar T.S. S/o Shivaraju, driver of the car No. KA-50-A-9858 for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.

17. In the Discharge Summary issued by NIMHANS, reason for the injuries are noted as alleged RTA, two wheeler vs. four wheeler on 02.08.2021 resulting in the head injuries.
18.
In this case, the respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve or rebut the evidence produced by PW.2 Sunitha regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.
In the file, evidence of the eye witness of the accident are not available.

Hence, I have concluded that on 02.08.2021 at 10.30 AM when petitioner was riding motorcycle No. KA-54-L-5977 by keeping Ramachandra on the pillion from Peenya towards Sahakarnagar on Hebbal Ring Road, near Hebbal Lake, Vinod Kumar S/o Shivaraju negligently drove the car No. KA-50-A-9858, dashed the same to motorcycle No.KA-54-L- 5977 thereby caused accident and caused injuries to the petitioner.

Hence,
I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative and Issue No.2 in the Negative.
19. Issue No.3:

In the evidence affidavit, PW.2 Sunitha stated that in the accident petitioner has suffered RT supra and Infra Tentone EDH with MLS, temporal bone fracture, CT Chest - Pneumothorax, took treatment at NIMHANS Hospital, then Mangala Hospital, Hassan as inpatient from 02.08.2021 to 07.08.2021, at the cost of Rs.2,50,000/-, produced medical bills worth of Rs.1,28,154/-.
20.
In the written statement, the respondent No.1 insurance company denied the allegations regarding the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
21. In the cross-examination P.W.2 stated that after hearing news of the accident went to NIMHANS Hospital.
PW.2 denied the suggestion that in order claim compensation she has admitted her husband to Mangala Hospital and created a discharge summary.
PW.2 denied the suggestion that as per wound certificate her husband has not suffered grievous injuries.
PW.2 denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.1,28,154/- towards treatment.
PW.2 denied the suggestion that she paid only Rs.57,350/- to the hospital for treatment.

sentences.text: In the evidence affidavit, PW.1 Dr.Shailesh C.V. Rao stated that on 09.01.2023 and 14.01.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that the petitioner suffered disability of 45% and produced OPD records, Skull X-ray report, Neuro Psychological Assessment Report, Mini Mental State Examination Report at Ex.P1 to P4.
In the cross-examination PW.1 stated that he never treated the petitioner and stated that on the basis of the Assessment of Disability deposed evidence.

23. Wound Certificate, Discharge Summary, medical bills, prescriptions, medical reports, Neuro Psychological Assessment Report and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered RT supra and Infra Tentone EDH with MLS, temporal bone fracture, CT Chest - Pneumothorax,, took treatment as inpatient at NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru from 02.08.2021 to 07.08.2021, then took treatment at Mangala Multi Speciality Hospital, Hassan from 26.08.2021 to 07.09.2021 by spending approximately at Rs.1,28,154/-.
In the copy of the Driving License marked at Ex.P14, date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 05.10.1987.

In the Neuro Psychological Assessment Report dated 12.01.2023 it is noted that the petitioner suffered his deformities in undertaking personal activities communication and understanding as well as the work which signifies several disabilities.
In the file, there are no documents regarding occupation and income of the petitioner.

24. In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve or rebut the evidence placed by PW.2 regarding the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by petitioner Nagaraju.

Hence, I have calculated the loss of future income, functional disability in the following manner: -
Sl. Particulars Amount in No. Rs.
a) Age of the petitioner as on the date of accident 34 years b) Monthly notional income of petitioner as 15,000/- on the date of accident c) 10% permanent functional disability 1,500/-
d) 1,500/- x 12 x 16 = 2,88,000/-
Hence, I award Rs.2,88,000/- towards loss of future income, Rs.1,25,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.1,28,154/- towards treatment charges, Rs.50,000/- towards attendant, nourishment and conveyance, Rs.1,50,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 10) towards loss of income during treatment period,
Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities and unhappiness.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled to receive Rs.8,41,154/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a. as compensation from the respondent No.1 and 2.
25.
In Para-5 of the written statement, the respondent No.1 insurance company admitted subsistence of the policy with respect to car No. KA-50-A-9858 as on the date of accident.

In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 owner of the car has Nagaraju vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72819845/
5 violated any terms of the policy.

sentences.text: Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 and 2 being insurer and owner of the car No. KA-50-A- 9858 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.8,41,154/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Forty One Thousand One Hundred Fifty Four only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.1 being the Insurer of the car No.KA-50-A-9858 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within three months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to the bank account PW.2 Sunitha W/o Nagaraju directly.

Surplus compensation amount and interest shall be deposited in any bank for a period of five years in the name of Nagaraju S/o Sonnajavare Gowda (Petitioner)
without creating any encumbrance with liberty to Sunitha wife of petitioner Nagaraju to withdraw periodical interest once in three months.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
